claim: GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds tracks the read position across all shards and consumers. If an iterator's age passes 50% of the retention period, records may expire before they are read, and a quick stopgap is to increase the retention period.

values.display: GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds

qualifiers.condition: default retention 24 hours, configurable up to 365 days

evidence.quote: Start with the `GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds` metric, which tracks the read position across all shards and consumers in the stream. Note that if an iterator's age passes 50% of the retention period (by default, 24 hours, configurable up to 365 days), there is risk for data loss due to record expiration. A quick stopgap solution is to increase the retention period.

claim: An exception thrown from processRecords is absorbed by the KCL, and the KCL does not resend that batch of records. Consumers then see skipped records, so all exceptions must be handled inside processRecords.
question: Why do records seem to be skipped by a KCL consumer?

values.display: does not resend the batch of records
absorbed by the KCL

evidence.quote: Any exception thrown from `processRecords` is absorbed by the KCL. To avoid infinite retries on a recurring failure, the KCL does not resend the batch of records processed at the time of the exception. The KCL then calls `processRecords` for the next batch of data records without restarting the record processor. This effectively results in consumer applications observing skipped records. To prevent skipped records, handle all exceptions within `processRecords` appropriately.

claim: A large producer that can micro-batch or buffer records should use the Kinesis Producer Library, the PutRecords operation, or aggregate records into a larger file before PutRecord. If it cannot batch, it should use multiple threads.

evidence.quote: If the customer can micro-batch/buffer records, use the [Amazon Kinesis Producer Library](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/dev/developing-producers-with-kpl.html) (which has advanced aggregation logic), the multi-record operation [PutRecords](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecords.html), or aggregate records into a larger file before using the single-record operation [PutRecord](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecord.html). If you are unable to batch/buffer, use multiple threads to write to the Kinesis Data Streams service at the same time.
